biography: Levi Simões hails from the vibrant, sun-drenched streets of Salvador, Bahia, Brazil. Growing up, the roar of engines was a constant soundtrack to his life, thanks to his father's small auto repair shop. Levi wasn't just watching; he was absorbing, learning the intricacies of mechanics from a young age. His racing journey began with karting at 12, quickly displaying a preternatural ability to analyze track conditions and exploit even the slightest advantage. A defining moment came during a regional karting championship where, despite starting last due to a mechanical failure, Levi meticulously picked off competitors one by one, clinching the victory with a daring last-corner overtake. This calculating approach has become his signature. Now at 26, Simões is a rising star, having founded his own small team, 'Levi Simoes,' showcasing his entrepreneurial spirit alongside his driving talent. While progress has been gradual, he is proving to be a canny and determined driver, always seeking improvement.
drivingStyle: Simões is a cerebral driver, known for his meticulous planning and data analysis. He doesn't rely on raw aggression; instead, he dissects each track, searching for the optimal racing line and braking points. His approach to corners is calculated and precise, prioritizing corner exit speed and tire conservation over flamboyant entries. He excels under pressure, maintaining composure when others crack, often using the mistakes of his rivals to his advantage. Tire management is a particular strength, enabling him to run longer stints and gain valuable positions in the later stages of a race.
rivalries: Ricardo Vargas - A fellow Brazilian driver known for his aggressive style, often clashing with Simões' calculated approach, leading to on-track incidents and heated exchanges.
Isabelle Dubois - A rising female driver with a similar analytical approach, creating a strategic rivalry where both seek to outsmart each other with data and setup choices.
Kenji Tanaka - A notoriously unpredictable driver whose daring maneuvers and disregard for convention frustrate Simões' meticulously planned strategies.
quirks: Always polishes his racing helmet with a special microfiber cloth before each session.
Listens to a specific playlist of Brazilian samba music while visualizing the track layout.
Carries a small, well-worn Senna quote card in his race suit.
famousQuote: Racing isn't about brute force; it's about understanding the dance between man, machine, and track.
careerHighlight: Winning the Brazilian National Karting Championship in 2018 after overcoming a significant points deficit in the final race.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of his debut single-seater race due to a misjudgment in wet conditions, resulting in significant damage to his car and a dent to his confidence.
